links.seed_title: Dipole Earth Magnetic Field and Solar Wind
links.seed_text: Dipole Earth Magnetic Field and Solar Wind: A textured Earth sphere with a tilted magnetic dipole generates looping field lines while a stream of charged-particle spheres (“solar wind”) flows in, gets deflected, trapped, or funneled along the lines, forming glowing auroral curtains at the poles.

links.seed_title: MRI-Style Strong Magnet With Human-Body Phantom
links.seed_text: MRI-Style Strong Magnet With Human-Body Phantom: A large cylindrical magnet creates a nearly uniform interior field drawn as parallel semi-transparent tubes passing through a simple human-body phantom, while labeled “spins” (tiny arrows) precess and gradually align with the field, emitting brief glowing pulses.

links.seed_title: Two Moving Bar Magnets With Dynamic Field Lines
links.seed_text: Two Moving Bar Magnets With Dynamic Field Lines: Two bar magnets on frictionless tracks can be dragged by the mouse, with their 3D field lines recalculating and smoothly morphing, showing attraction/repulsion as lines merge, bulge, and pinch, with color gradients indicating field strength.

links.seed_title: Bar Magnet With Iron Filings Field Lines
links.seed_text: Bar Magnet With Iron Filings Field Lines: A central 3D bar magnet creates animated magnetic field lines drawn as curved glowing tubes while hundreds of tiny iron-filing rods float, rotate, and then align and cluster along the lines, with a light background and color-coded poles.

links.seed_title: Current-Carrying Wire and Circular Field Lines
links.seed_text: Current-Carrying Wire and Circular Field Lines: A long vertical wire with animated current arrows creates concentric circular magnetic field lines drawn as rotating rings; test charges orbit or spiral along these rings, leaving fading trails that show their curved paths.

links.seed_title: Magnetic Field of a Circular Loop Coil
links.seed_text: Magnetic Field of a Circular Loop Coil: A horizontal current loop (or solenoid segment) generates donut-shaped and arching field lines; floating compass needles (short arrows) drift, rotate, and then lock onto the local field direction, with labels and field strength color bars.
